title: introduce-sideband-trace-anchors-and-interactive-cost-slices
author: Maya Ortiz
description: Motivation: long-tail cost/latency investigations frequently require stitching token-level billing with partial traces and UI workflows. This PR adds two complementary capabilities: 1) sideband trace anchors — lightweight deterministic anchors emitted at routing time that let downstream logs/metrics link back to a canonical trace without full baggage, enabling high-cardinality joins at query time; 2) interactive cost slices — a server-side metric rollup and UI surface that computes per-request per-segment cost/latency slices (prefix, gen, streaming) and exposes small sparkline payloads for quick triage. This change includes schema updates for the anchor token, an opt-in rollout flag and migration path, new rollout-canary dashboards, and an alert tuning recipe that reduces alert noise using an adaptive exponential smoothing step for token-cost anomalies. Checklist: - add anchor generator and deterministic anchor id (opt-in) - extend trace ingestion pipeline to index anchor field (backfill-friendly) - implement cost-slice rollup proto and server aggregator - expose compact sparklines in the console and raw CSV export - add automated regression test for anchor collision rate < 1e-8 - document rollout notes and opt-out controls Rollout plan: enable opt-in for 5% of requests for 48h, evaluate collision and join latency, then 25% -> 100% with migration job to backfill anchors for 30 days of historical traces. Related: ENG-5213 (investigate long-tail billing noise), ENG-5378 (console mini-sparklines).

review_comments: Kenji Sato: Opt-in makes sense. Please confirm anchor entropy on low-token requests — observed potential duplication in tests.

release_notes: Adds sideband trace anchors for low-cost trace-to-log joins, server-side interactive cost slices with compact sparklines in the console, and an alert tuning recipe to reduce token-cost anomaly noise. Includes opt-in rollout and migration guidance.
